subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, agent turn completion, and tool-call-threshold lifecycle data to workspace/internal hooks, or keep that data behind typed plugin hooks?
rationale: The missing surface is source-proven, but the safe payload, permission boundary, event ordering, and threshold configuration semantics are public API and security choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
options.body: Add narrow workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion with minimized payloads, while keeping mutation and mid-turn control in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Plugin-Only Lifecycle Surface
options.body: Treat existing typed plugin hooks as the supported lifecycle API and document that HOOK.md workspace hooks are not for sensitive run lifecycle data.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one combined lifecycle model covering internal hooks, plugin hooks, payload redaction, ordering, and thresholds.

recommendation.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
recommendation.body: Add narrow workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion with minimized payloads, while keeping mutation and mid-turn control in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on typed hook contracts and lifecycle/security boundaries where recent related hook-contract work points most strongly.
